look_here_first: Usually upright/ascending and hairy, with alternate lanceolate leaves and typically 5 yellow petals plus 10 stamens; confirm long hairy bumpy capsules.

morphology_keys.habit: Erect to ascending, often hairy, branching wetland herb; some parts may become woody.
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate, lanceolate and often visibly hairy, commonly short-petioled.
morphology_keys.flower: Typically 5 (occasionally 4, 6 or 7) yellow petals with stamens twice the sepal number.
morphology_keys.fruit: Long narrow thin-walled hairy capsule, usually marked by small bumps corresponding to seeds.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Against Ludwigia peploides, usually upright and hairy rather than shiny-leaved floating mat; inspect elongated hairy capsule. Against octovalvis, typical 5-merous flowers vs 4.
